## Course structure {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}

- Why good SE matters in research
- How to apply these everyday to write higher quality code
  - Core principles
  - Key tools
  - Useful techniques

::: 

::: {.column width="10%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

- Tooling for better research software 
  - venv for virtual environments
  - formatting and linting - best practices
  - structuring code
- Writing better research software 
  - comments and docstrings 
  - repository documentation - licenses, README
  - Other (naming, magic numbers,...)

:::

# RSE Skills Day 2 {.smaller}

Jack Atkinson and Marion Weinzierl

ICCS RSE

## RSE Skills - Day 2 {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="65%"}

Welcome back.

Today we will cover making software easier to read and use through:

- comments,
- documentation,
- naming, and
- repository structuring.

\

## Other things {.smaller}

Beyond the scope of today are a few other honourable mentions:

- Functions and modules
- Packaging
  - Breaking projects into modules and `__init__.py`
  - Distributing projects with `pyproject.toml`
- Documentation
  - Auto-generation from docstrings with sphinx or mkdocs
- Type hinting
  - Adding type hinting to python code - how and why?
  - Type checking with mypy

These lessons are beyond the scope of today.

<!-- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -->

# Closing


## Where can I get help? {.smaller}

If you would like to discuss applying this to your own codebase consider signing up for
an ICCS Climate Code Clinic:

- 1hr slot
- RSEs will review code in advance and provide feedback and guidance.
- [Online booking form](https://iccs.cam.ac.uk/resources-vesri-members/climate-code-clinic)

There is also the option of booking in all week during the summer school via the
[Booking Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1v8y2GodI9JZoHrFRpLW2tD135MurDBMIcr-ArBFIT3A/edit?usp=sharing).

\

We will also be available during the mini-project slots on Thursday to help you apply
these principles to any code, existing or new.
